refactor(onchain,sdk): single-anchor multi-field opening; retire committed-source transaction_commitment (#584)

Phase-5 follow-up, first of the two compiled-surface blockers ahead of
#579's single blueprint regeneration.

Single-anchor opening: field-opening-v1.ak gains an opaque
AnchoredNativeTxV1 handle (anchored_native_tx pays the tx-id derivation
and witness_set_hash check once) with anchored_field_view /
anchored_field_walk opening N fields against one anchor. Every opening
re-runs both guards - carriage_reaches_the_anchor and the §2.5
body/witness pairing - as separate expects so a refusal names its guard.
resolved_sources is deleted; opened_field_view/walk are thin wrappers, so
the guards have one spelling. The handle deliberately exposes no
witness_set_hash accessor (the #575 forgery class), and the validity-code
accessor is named unanchored_validity_code_of because that is what it is.
transition-trace's validate_l2_transaction_transition builds one handle
for its three body fields: Q21 L2 row 2,760,481 -> 2,334,205 mem (8%
under the 2,533,821 AC ceiling), forced-order row 3,034,025 -> 2,538,180.
Q31/Q1x single-field rows rose +7,117/+7,580 mem per opening (routing
through the handle + the guard split); re-measured, cause recorded in all
three exec ledgers, under 0.06% of the §3.3 basis.

Committed-source retirement: transaction_commitment leaves
L2TransactionSourceV1 and ForcedInclusionTxV1 (leaf value was always a
pure function of source; the L1 mint-time derivation check in
material_directory still pins TxOrderPayloadV1's copy, and
validation-claim-v1 re-anchors NormalValidationSource by deriving
source_proof_commitment directly - same value, same binding, one
derivation per claim as before). SDK twin and ~25 producer/reader sites
move in step; goldens regenerated on both language sides
(transaction-root-v1 fixture pair, transition-trace-abi.json,
ValidationSourceMembershipV1 corpus bf590321 -> 5cba4fd7, tx-order CBOR
vectors); format-registry arity pins 4 -> 3; tex/consensus-profile docs
updated. TxOrderPayloadV1 / TxFieldPreimageV1 / TxFieldReceiptV1 keep
their copies by design.

Verification: field_opening_v1 27/27 (three new second-open tier-guard
rows), transition-trace proof 38/38, full Aiken suite byte-identical 34
pre-existing failures vs HEAD, q21/q31/q1x/carriage exec-ledger
verifiers pass without --update, sdk-aiken-schema-parity 32/32 against a
scratch-built blueprint, TS suites green across sdk/node/watcher/
da-committee/fault-proofs. plutus.json untouched
(c52589df225145ad74c8f444d500dfe5): ten tests (six emulator, four
schema-parity rows) are red against the stale in-tree blueprint until
#579 regenerates it - the accepted price of the ordering, with the exact
set recorded at the blueprint load sites for #579's implementer.
Three review rounds (1 major + 9 minors, then 1 major + 5 minors, then
CLEAN); parent-only surfaces untouched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs(core,sdk): name the counted-scheme residual at the nine-field consumer call sites (#578)

Phase-5 lane D: the anticipated family-directory claim was empty - the
field-6 native-script family is Q17 missing-native-script-tx, which #575
took inside its Q10-Q19 block, and an audit of all sixteen directories
under validators/fraud-proofs/ (independently re-verified in review) found
no unclaimed directory left on counted-scheme access (Q20 min-fee already
reads through the door; Q44 da-hash-preimage frames the compact tx, not
per-field items; mpf-chunked-proof is clean).

Lane D therefore claimed the one surface the wave flagged repeatedly and
no lane took: the nine-field TypeScript consumer path. The flat swap was
attempted for real and measured - four lines changed, dists rebuilt,
every package diffed against its own baseline: 58 new failures across
four packages, rooted in two structural blockers (the counted per-item
publication receipt chain in consensus-validation-v1.ts with live
consumers in midgard-node/midgard-sdk, and the §5.3/§5.6 item grammar
never re-pointed in the TS producers). The swap was reverted as
worse-than-either-end and the work re-homed to #585, which now blocks
#579 via a native tracker edge (alongside #584, whose missing edge was
also recorded).

What lands in-tree is the honest residual: docstring annotations at
deriveNativeTxBodyCompact / deriveNativeTxWitnessSetCompact and the
zero-input fraud-proof builder naming the counted/flat gap at the call
sites, with one authoritative note (native-body.ts) and pointers from the
siblings, plus a durable test title asserting the counted-scheme empty
spend-inputs hash. Semantic inertness proven by AST comment-strip: three
files byte-identical after stripping, the fourth differs only in the
it() title.

#578's issue body carries a Deviation section with an AC-applicability
table: AC1 met (claim recorded, disjoint, audit confirmed), AC2 re-homed
to #585, AC3 provably N/A (no .ak change, no execution row owed), AC4
restated as no-regression (fork full check 1707/34 = HEAD's identical
failure set; the ten red Aiken tests are #585's exit criteria, pinned by
name there).

Verification: midgard-core 460/460; midgard-sdk 237/238 (single
pre-existing blueprint-drift failure owned by #579); tsc/eslint/prettier
clean; core+sdk dists rebuilt; stock v1.1.22 compile exit 0; zero .ak
files touched so the fork baseline holds by construction. Two review
rounds (2 majors + 8 minors, then LAND with 5 prose minors); parent-only
surfaces untouched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(onchain): rebind Q21 transition-trace onto the authenticated field door (#577)

Phase-5 lane C: the transition-trace family (Q21) now consumes body fields
exclusively through the §8.8 authenticated_field_view door via the #575
FieldOpeningV1 bridge (opened_field_walk + fold_opened_field with
BodyFieldOpening/BodyAnchor{tx_id}). The inherited WIP's direct
open_field_walk call with a hand-rolled unread witness set is gone; both
rebound sites sit behind carriage_reaches_the_anchor and the §2.5 pairing.
Counted-scheme codec twins and the proof-step witness idiom
(verify_native_tx_proof_source_v1 / native_tx_proof_commitment_v1) are
deleted from the claimed directory; the door's §5.4 aggregate byte cap is
gained in the exchange. Two redundant transaction_commitment comparisons
were dropped only after proving their value pinned elsewhere (MPF membership
on the L2 side, tx-order NFT reference input on the forced side).

Disjoint single-writer lane: claimed only Q21 transition-trace, disjoint
from #575 (Q1x) and #576 (Q31); claim recorded on the issue before work.

New Q21 exec ledger at the 13.2M basis: forced-order path -5.0%
(3,194,009 -> 3,034,025 mem), L2 path +8.9% (2,533,821 -> 2,760,481 mem).
The regression's cause is exact and disclosed - first script in the wave to
open two fields, so the tx id is re-derived three times; the multi-field
opening that fixes it is filed as #584, blocking #579. Neutralisation set
re-derived by mutation: 5 selectors / 4 mutations, each with a distinct red
set.

Ledger tooling consolidated: new shared exec-ledger-within-basis-v1 checker
(exported GOAL_SPEC_EXECUTION_BASIS_V1 constant, zero-row refusal, named
shape errors, 12-case self-test) consumed by the Q21 and migrated Q31
verifiers; q1x/carriage verifiers keep their derived-row shape but now take
the basis from the shared constant and refuse zero-row runs - all guards
negatively probed. All four ledgers get uniform CI pin steps, the two
compile-free self-tests are hoisted above every fallible step, and the
pre-existing normalized-fmt drift is fixed at root cause (9 files from
landed tickets; reformat byte-identical under stock v1.1.22 and fork
v1.1.23+2a78108, fixed point under both, all four ledgers re-verified to
the unit afterwards). Epoch-645 basis provenance corrected in three ledgers
per GOAL_SPEC §3.3.

Fork-runner: family suite 38/38 (+3 new vectors); full check 2301 checks /
34 errors = HEAD's identical failure set, none in transition_trace. Stock
v1.1.22 compiles clean; normalized fmt clean. Survived three review rounds
(1 major + 9 minor, then 3 major + 6 minor, then LAND with 7 pre-existing
or cosmetic minors); parent-only surfaces untouched, deferred exactly to
#584 -> #579.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(onchain): rebind Q31 reference-input-no-idx onto the authenticated field door (#576)

Phase-5 lane B: the reference-input-no-idx family (Q31) now threads the
disputed transaction's id instead of its field commitments, opening field 1
(reference inputs) and field 2 (outputs) through the §10 authenticated_field_view
door via the #575 FieldOpeningV1 idiom. Steps 01→02 thread verified_tx_id and
03→04 thread producing_tx_id; step-02 opens field 1 with spend_input_at (field 1
shares field 0's 38-byte stride), step-04 reads field 2 via field_item_count.
Both are body fields (0-5), so BodyAnchor{tx_id} covers them — the family
touches no witness field, so no WitnessAnchor and no tier-3 Certified exposure.
Counted-scheme field access (bounded_collection_v1 / bounded_item_v1 /
field_commitment_from_items) and the proof-source idiom are gone from the
family's directories.

Disjoint single-writer lane: claimed only Q31, leaving the shared
transition-trace / validation-machine surface and the TS consumer path for
other lanes.

New Q31 exec ledger at the 13.2M basis (step-02 1,849,702 mem, step-04
1,832,278 mem — both ~14%, basisFit:"within"); no new unbounded walk, so no
"exceeds" row. Verifier's --update absorbs measurement drift but fails on
structural failure (mutation-verified).

Fork-runner: family suites 10/10; full check 2298 checks / 34 errors = HEAD
baseline, zero new failures, none in the family. Stock v1.1.22 compiles clean;
normalized-format clean on all six authored files. The prepare-reference-input-no-idx
off-chain builder stays on the counted-era ABI, deferred to #579's blueprint
regeneration exactly as #575 left its input-no-idx twin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(onchain): rebind Q1x fraud-proof families onto the authenticated field door (#575)

Phase-5 first wave: the ten Q1x families (Q10-Q19) now thread the disputed
transaction's id — not one of its nine field commitments — and re-derive the
tx-id-verified compact structures at each step, opening every field through
the §10 authenticated_field_view door. New field-opening-v1 idiom makes §2.5's
body/witness split structural (BodyFieldOpening 0-5 / WitnessFieldOpening 6-8)
and constructs the unread witness set internally so no prover-fillable argument
exists for a field the door won't read. Deletes the last free-standing-hash
consumer (double-spend/input-witness.ak) and retires common.ak's now-dead
verify_native_tx_witness_set.

Security: fields 6-8 (witness set) are not covered by §3's tx-id preimage, so
the rebind threads a NativeTxAnchorV1 (BodyAnchor{tx_id} | WitnessAnchor{tx_id,
witness_set_hash}) from the MPF-anchored step-01 and checks the door-derived
witness_set_hash against it — closing a slashing-forgery path where a prover
could bind an honest transaction's witness field to a fabricated preimage.
Tier-3 Certified carriage is refused for fields 6-8 (carriage_reaches_the_anchor)
because the §8.6 certificate binds content to the uncommitted trailing hash;
the durable wire fix (fold the field commitment into the asset name) is assigned
to #579. Both closures carry both-direction neutralisation vectors. §8.3
erratum E2 records the completeness limit this trades for.

AC ledger: new Q1x exec ledger at the 13.2M basis (16 rows / 8 derived),
covering both unbounded walks the rebind introduces (Q17 step-06 field 6, Q16
step-04 field 7) as loud basisFit:"exceeds" rows requiring an infeasibility
string + E2 cross-ref, neither --update-rewritable; both exec-ledger verifiers
hardened so --update absorbs measurement drift but never structural failure.
Q1X-F6 measured under flat and posted provisional-expected-resolved to #551
(not reopened). Per-lifecycle-step re-measurement is Phase-7's against the
Phase-6 blueprint.

Fork-runner: full check 1702 tests / 34 failures — zero new vs the 1677/41
HEAD baseline; 7 retired counted-scheme tests removed with their machinery.
Both exec ledgers pass. Off-chain builders knowingly stale against the new step
ABI (redeemer/datum shapes + certificate policy param) and deferred to #579's
blueprint regeneration, marked at every live route.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(core,sdk,onchain): publish/heal tooling + carriage exit measurements (#574)

Publish/heal tooling for §8 carriage: planner/healer/lay-out in midgard-core
(tier a total function of length, invisible to consumers), publication/
certification/retirement builders in midgard-sdk, end-to-end emulator suite —
including heal by a second unrelated wallet with the original certificate, a
hostile wrong-bytes publication, a full-K chunk yank, and a certificate really
minted on the ledger. TS twin for the frozen §8.6 mint redeemer + a third
cross-language golden channel (10 positive vectors incl. 63/64/65-byte Plutus
Data boundary cases, 17 negative vectors; Aiken side decodes AND re-serialises;
CI-gated).

Headline: §8.3 erratum E1 — K = 15,900 is falsified by signed-tx framing. A
full chunk publishes as 16,648 B against maxTxSize 16,384 (+264). Measured
frontiers at 1-byte resolution: 15,644 exact / 15,148 with the 512 B reserve;
outage window (15,148, 32,768] — tier 3 is inoperative on L1 until #565
re-pins K (serialized surface; constant deliberately unchanged, divergence
stated). Tooling now fails closed by default: byte-exact cost model
(245 B fixed + datum head + Plutus-Data payload encoding, pinned against real
signed transactions), publishability guard, refusing builder. Like-for-like
capacity vs the counted era corrected to +155 B at both frontiers. Tier-1
wire-cost caution (14,786 B for a 14,336 B preimage) recorded. §8.10 ledgers
the carriage measurements; its 13 execution figures are pinned by a new
CI-wired exec ledger (neutralisation selectors required non-empty). §9 records
that Lucid's Data.from is not fail-closed on trailing bytes.

AC-1's full-cap half is explicitly deferred to #565 (E1 "What #574 discharges,
and what it defers"); everything else discharged with executable evidence.

Fork-runner green: carriage 34, wire-golden 42, handlers 32, field-access 127;
TS: core 460/460, sdk 237/238, validation 253/255 (3 pre-existing failures:
2 stale plutus.json awaiting #579, 1 #571 scanner-consumer gap). Exec-ledger
gate green (13 rows, 9 derived, binding axis cpu).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(onchain): permissionless chunk-certificate validator + fixed-K chunking (#573)

Producer half of the §8 carriage ladder: native-tx-carriage-v1 with
deterministic fixed-K split (K = 15,900, aggregate cap 32,768, reproducible
from bytes alone — pinned against the cross-language straddle golden vector),
chunk digests, producer certificate twin, and the §8.6 content predicate that
re-derives the binding tx id via §3 (never trusts the redeemer). New
field-preimage-certificate validator: permissionless mint (Certify/Retire) +
spend, token name = content address, single-asset single-pair output at the
script address with inline datum, no stake credential, no reference script;
burn stated over outputs (double-satisfaction-proof); healable by an unrelated
party (handler-level test). §8.6 freezes the mint-redeemer wire format for
#574's off-chain twin, records the certificate output shape, and adds the
wiring constraint that certificate_policy_id must be a compile-time validator
parameter. Comment-only note in native-tx-field-access-v1 documents the
chunk-shape divergence; consolidation deferred to the #565 serialized patch.

Fork-runner green: carriage 25/25, handlers 24/24; full native_tx machine lane
re-verified (field-access 105+22+62, machine-walk 46, intra-item 52,
fault-statement 48, script-pushdown 32). Stock v1.1.22 compile clean;
plutus.json deliberately stale by one script — identity cascade lands in #579.
Tier-boundary and reorder guards neutralisation-pinned (each turns exactly its
named vector red).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(onchain): witness-minimal fault statements + tier-2 re-hash exit measurement (#572)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(onchain): intra-item package — Value bookmark, Canonical-Data Acceptor, native-script pushdown (#571)

The Phase-3b intra-item access package, worked as one unit in the machine
lane, plus §11 written into docs/spec/midgard-tx.md — the section #566
reserved and #570 deliberately did not encroach on.

Case A — Value bookmark (native-tx-intra-item-v1.ak). Ordered intra-item
access into a multiasset value without materialising the output. 64 lookups
over 8 policies x 8 assets cost 12.22M mem against the 13,200,000-mem
GOAL_SPEC §3.3 basis; the materialising control costs 20.15M and does not
fit. The two are pinned to the same 64 answers, so the comparison means
something. The gap decomposes as 6.10M fixed plus 1.83M marginal — recorded
that way rather than as a single headline, because the fixed decode dominates
and `decode_canonical_output` also decides datum and script_ref, which the
bookmark never inspects.

Case B — Canonical-Data Acceptor. Datum interior access at 0.93M and 4.87M,
both far inside the basis. Reported honestly: the `cbor.deserialise` controls
are cheaper (0.18M / 1.07M) with no crossover at width, since deserialise is
a builtin and the acceptor is interpreted. Case B is a capability case, not a
cost case, and §11.4 says so — an earlier "materialisation is priced by the
whole item" claim was removed because the measurement refutes it for datums.

The capability is real, and it closes #567's residual. #567 screened
top-level bignum-headed datums with a head-byte check and documented that
nested bignums — canonical at any depth — still aborted the script, deferring
the fix here. Under PV11 `ConstrData` takes a Word64, and Aiken stdlib's
`cbor.deserialise` computes `ix = tag - 121` with no range guard, so any CBOR
tag below 121 aborts. The recursive acceptor now declines instead, verified
for a bignum as a map key, first-in-list, mid-list, at depth 5, and inside
tag-102. `is_canonical_plutus_data_v1`'s verdict is provably unchanged, so
L1 parity and #567's AC4 hold: canonical and materialisable stay separate
questions.

Case C — native-script checkpointable pushdown. Traversal 1.42M, checkpoint
and resume 1.79M, recursive-checker control 1.26M. The cursor is 87 bytes,
constant across scripts, `pub opaque` with a private decoder and only the
commitment-taking resume exported — #570's §10.6 shape preserved.

Two consensus divergences from the definitional checker, both caught by
review and both fixed
- The depth bound counted frames where `native_script_v1` counts nodes with a
  leaf at depth 1, so the pushdown admitted depth 17 while the checker refused
  it. On 16 nested `all` around one signature the checker returned None and
  the pushdown returned Some(True). Fixed with an explicit
  `max_native_script_frames = max_native_script_depth - 1`, and the agreement
  test now spans depths 1, 2, 15 and 16 rather than stopping at 3, with the
  other side pinned so the fix cannot over-refuse.
- `required` carried an upper bound the definition does not have, so
  `at_least(33, [signature])` — which the checker evaluates to Some(False) —
  aborted instead. A script the definition calls invalid could not be
  adjudicated at all. `required` is now capped rather than bounded: anything
  above the node count maps onto `unsatisfiable_required`, which preserves the
  verdict because `satisfied` can never reach it, while keeping the frame's
  wire scalar three bytes wide.

Guard coverage follows §9.5's discipline. §11.5 enumerates 36 refusals — 29
isolated, 7 backstops — reconciled against the 71 `expect` sites in the new
modules, with every backstop proven by neutralisation rather than argued. The
first recount said 15; auditing found 21 more, including one whose stated
"checked one step earlier" rebuttal was simply false.

Also fixed in review: the cursor's array header spelled `88` over seven
elements, so the wire form was not decodable CBOR — now `87`, with a test
that decodes it; the resume test could not detect a restart-from-zero, now
budgeted at exactly the remaining work and pinned both ways;
`datum_alternative_at_v1` aborted where §11 promises None, now guarded like
its two siblings; and the §5.6 citations for an output-value name cap were
re-pointed to §5.5, which now states the basis it was missing.

Note for future neutralisation work: deleting a guard whose constrained value
has no other consumer makes Aiken erase the whole computation, which reddens
many tests for the wrong reason. Weaken the predicate instead.

Verification: fork suite 2112 checks / 47 errors from a 2028/47 baseline
established by a detached worktree at 92fcffda, with the failing-NAME set
byte-identical — none of the 47 cleared, none added. Stock aiken check
--skip-tests: 0 errors. All seven touched .ak files are aiken fmt clean;
#570's modules were not touched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(onchain): machine walk core — authenticate-once, walk-derived item access, resumable checkpoints (#570)

The Phase-3a machine walk. Lazy per-field authenticate-once against the flat
hash, then three-tier offset-and-slice item access with no offset table: every
read is walk-derived from the authenticated bytes themselves, so there is no
second data structure to trust or dispute. Resumable checkpoints carry
positions, never bytes.

New lib/midgard/native-tx-machine-walk-v1.ak, plus §10 written into
docs/spec/midgard-tx.md (§10.1–§10.8), which #566 reserved for this ticket.

Measured, not asserted
- Authenticate-once (AC1): one open serving 64 reads costs 8,782,831 mem;
  re-opening the door per item costs 13,275,371 — over the 13,200,000-mem
  GOAL_SPEC §3.3 basis. Authenticate-once is what puts a 64-item field walk
  inside a transaction, with 33% headroom. Holding relocation constant and
  varying only door-opens gives 9,790,000 vs 13,275,371, so the verdict is not
  a fixture artifact; the 4.49M gap decomposes as ~3.48M door-opens plus
  ~1.01M access pattern, and all four rows now ship as tests so §10.7's
  re-take is reproducible from the suite.
- Arithmetic slice (AC3): spend_input_at at index 0 costs 7,827,953 mem and at
  index 295 costs 7,828,553 — 600 units across 295 positions, assertion
  residue. The variable-width control costs 59,704 mem per index step, about
  29,400x.

Resume carries positions only (AC2). A walk pauses at item 7 of 20 and resumes
in a follow-on transaction under a different carriage tier with a budget of
exactly the 13 remaining items, so a walk that restarted at zero would run
short; the both-ways pin confirms one fewer fails. Two preimages with the same
widths and disjoint content walked to the same position produce byte-identical
53-byte checkpoints.

A redeemer-controlled position hole, closed structurally
- resume_field_walk originally took a plain checkpoint argument, letting a
  caller supply a prover-chosen position — and a variable-width position is
  not recomputable, so nothing downstream could catch it. Making that function
  private was not enough: FieldWalkCheckpointV1 was a plain pub type, so its
  constructor was exported and walk_next/walk_skip/walk_fold accepted any
  checkpoint. A probe using only the public API built a literal checkpoint at
  offset 5 and read bytes from inside an item's payload with no commitment
  check at all.
- The type is now pub opaque and the decoder is private, so a position can only
  be derived, advanced, or returned by the commitment-checked resume. The probe
  no longer compiles. §10.6 and the module header now state exactly what the
  type system enforces, and separately what a library cannot enforce — where
  the caller's committed digest comes from, which stays normative on dispute
  entry points.

Guard coverage is now a property, not a claim
- Six guards documented in §10 had zero coverage: their negative vectors were
  tripping a deeper guard first, so the named guard could have been deleted
  with CI still green. Every refusal was audited by neutralising it one at a
  time and requiring exactly one test to go red.
- §10.8 enumerates all 23 refusals: 16 with isolating vectors, 7 as backstops
  that are unreachable-as-refusers, each naming the earlier check that makes it
  so. §9.5 admits exactly those two categories — uncovered is not one.
- Related: seven fail vectors were first written as `let _x = guard(...)`,
  which Aiken erases entirely, so none of them ran. Every negative now consumes
  its guard's result.
- v1_c20_script_item_does_not_open_as_field_7 was green for the wrong reason —
  a 34-byte item can never satisfy field 7's stride, so it was refused by the
  wrapper check rather than by the field hash. Rebuilt from a structurally
  valid 101-byte item so only the hash comparison can refuse it; neutralising
  that comparison now turns both directions red.

Scope
- 34 of the 37 counted-opening reds are deferred with cause: the 27
  validation-machine failures are control-type redesigns across 15 verify_item
  and 20 verify_chunk sites whose datums thread item_count/item_index/
  chunk_index/frontier into successor encodings (the machine lane, #572 AC4),
  and the 7 input-no-idx failures are Q13 (#575 AC1). Neither is a call-site
  swap. The 3 user_events/tx_order_v1 reds are owned by no ticket and are
  raised separately rather than deferred again.

Verification: fork suite 2028 checks / 47 errors from a 1983/48 baseline. The
failing-NAME set was diffed against a rebuilt HEAD state, not just counted:
exactly one cleared (the intended C20 rebind) and zero added. Stock aiken check
--skip-tests: 0 errors. §11 correctly absent — it is #571's.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(core,onchain): per-field cross-language golden vectors for all nine fields (#569)

The Phase-2 tail: per-field golden-vector suites over the sum-type twins,
extending #568's channel rather than reinventing it.

New surface
- demo/midgard-core/src/codec/native-tx-field-items-v1.ts — the nine per-field
  §5.3 item encoders and §5.1 per-field preimage producers, TS twins of
  preimages.ak / components.ak. Fields 2 and 6 reuse the existing canonical
  encoders rather than re-spelling them.
- A second generated channel (generator + vector definitions + JSON fixture +
  a 62-test Aiken module), wired to package scripts and the CI gate exactly as
  #568's is, with the shared tail factored into scripts/golden-channel.mjs.

Coverage: each field gets envelope, §4 commitment, header, extents and reads,
plus a producer round-trip — the only cross-language proof available for
fields 2 and 5, whose items are whole records. Boundaries: fixed indices
0/23/24/255/256/65535, the two-byte header at 24 items, the MidgardV1 tag
18 80, all seven purpose tags, mint ordering including burns, and §6.2
bignum/constr-128 datums pinned as bytes — never deserialised, since under
PV11 they are canonical but not materialisable.

The straddle vector was pinning an unreachable configuration

fix(onchain): enforce the pexcludes non-membership proof

`validators/pexcludes.ak` bound `mpf.insert` with `let _excluded`. Aiken fully
ignores unused let-bindings, so the call -- and the `expect excluding(key,
proof) == self.root` inside it, which IS the non-membership proof -- was
compiled away. The `exclusion` validator fell through to `True` for any
`[root, key, proof]` redeemer of the right shape, so a prover could forge a
non-existent-input fraud proof against a valid block and slash an honest
operator.

Bind with `expect`, the form already used at
`lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/transition-trace/proof.ak:671`.

The compiled withdraw script goes from 374 to 2977 bytes: the proof walk
previously occupied zero bytes on chain. Measured against a pristine build of
the same commit with the same compiler, exactly five validators move --
`pexcludes.exclusion` plus the four steps that embed its hash constant
(`no_input/step_03`, `no_input/step_04`, `no_reference_input/step_03`,
`no_reference_input/step_04`).

  pexcludes.exclusion  5a06db38b22c52ca7d1789f16c1819da03b15171efe245ef18ad7af6
                    -> a9ec251d6476217b1abccd5f035dec1272a4b04f640f503fca9e734d

`plutarch_pexcludes*` locates the withdraw redeemer *by* that constant, so the
pin move is required for the fix to take effect. Both `env/default.ak` and
`env/testnet.ak` are updated and re-verified against real builds of each env.

Adds the first tests this validator has ever had: a bogus proof against an
unproven root must be rejected (this test fails on the unfixed validator), and
a genuine non-membership witness must still be accepted. The defect survived
because the delegating steps only field-match the redeemer -- all cryptography
lived here, and nothing exercised it.

Gates: full typecheck clean; dual-compiler blueprint agreement clean (393
validators byte-identical across stock v1.1.22 and fork v1.1.23); pexcludes and
both delegating families pass. The §4.4 journey regression has NOT been run.

Pre-existing defect from dbfa7426; unrelated to #567.

feat(onchain): flat field-hash core scheme swap — nine flat commitments, one field-access door, canonicity re-pin (#567)

All nine compact-tx per-field commitments become flat blake2b-256 over raw
canonical enveloped field-preimage bytes, per docs/spec/midgard-tx.md.

The one door
- New lib/midgard/native-tx-field-access-v1.ak exposes the single
  authenticated_field_view: slice-only, straddle-aware, serving all three
  carriage tiers over FieldCarriageV1 (Inline/RawUtxo/Certified) and
  FieldViewV1 (Whole/Chunked) with lazy chunk verify. Positional hash
  extraction is private, so no caller can supply a free-standing field hash.
- bounded_collection_v1.from_items and codec.encode_native_byte_list removed;
  87 call sites rebound. verify_spend_inputs_preimage and spend_input_cbor_at
  deleted. One surviving production free-standing-hash consumer,
  input-witness.verified_spend_inputs_at, is documented and owned by the
  #575-#578 family rebind.
- One strict §5.1 header reader (minimal width, 9a rejected) now serves all
  eight envelope sites including mint; codec's general-CBOR reader keeps only
  its non-§5.1 role.

Preimage grammar
- Fixed 3-byte 19 XXXX output index; every other spelling rejected, so spend
  inputs are 38-byte items at stride 40. Mint moves off the raw map to the
  enveloped policy-item list. Fields 3/4 assert 28 bytes.
- Fixed-stride accessors now decode each item's own wrapper header rather than
  deriving the extent arithmetically. Without this, 81 ‖ 00 00 ‖ <28B> and
  81 ‖ ff ff ‖ <38B> opened through the door at byte-identical cost to the
  canonical spelling — two admissible commitments for one logical content,
  against §6.1. Both counterexamples are now regression vectors.
- Tier 3 enforces the §8.4 boundary (preimage_len > K) instead of merely
  total_length > 0, and field_item_count aborts for a variable-width tier-3
  view rather than returning the header's unauthenticated number.

Canonicity re-pin
- New lib/midgard/canonical-plutus-data-v1.ak re-pins the predicate to
  serialiseData's image: bignum tags 2/3 and constr tag 102 are canonical,
  restoring L1 parity.
- The materialisation path screens bignum-headed datums so it declines rather
  than aborting. This is deliberately separate from the canonicity predicate:
  bignums are canonical, they just cannot be materialised through the stdlib
  decoder at protocol version 11, where ConstrData takes a Word64 and the
  decoder's ix = tag - 121 goes negative. Nested bignums remain canonical at
  any depth and still abort; the residual is documented, not papered over, and
  belongs to #571's Canonical-Data Acceptor.
